nature_md: Meta paid ~$14.3B for a 49% **non-voting** stake in Scale AI (June 2025, ~$29B valuation) — quasi-M&A structured to avoid control and merger review. The deal's real payload was talent: founder-CEO Alexandr Wang left to run Meta's superintelligence effort (with a small group of Scale employees), while Scale continued as a nominally independent company under interim CEO Jason Droege. Fallout was immediate: Google, OpenAI, and xAI paused or wound down data-labeling work with Scale, cutting into the revenue base Meta had just paid for.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Non-voting 49% stake — Meta does not consolidate Scale; carried as an equity investment (equity method or fair value depending on rights). The effective price of Wang and team is embedded in the investment, not expensed as compensation.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Primary/secondary proceeds to Scale and its shareholders — financing, not revenue. Counterweight: customer attrition (Google/OpenAI/xAI) directly reduced post-deal revenue, a key input to whether the ~$29B mark holds.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** $14.3B for a non-voting half of a services firm whose top customers left on announcement — the price was for one person and looks like acqui-hire inflation at record scale. **Bull:** frontier-model data pipelines are a strategic bottleneck; Meta secured the category leader's capacity and its founder while leaving antitrust surface area minimal (CNBC, Forbes coverage).

events.title: Meta takes 49% non-voting stake in Scale AI; Alexandr Wang departs for Meta
